newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Amoco denies reports it pulling out of Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Amoco denies reports it pulling out of Colombia.

text.p: The head of Amoco's Colombian subsidiary denied a published report saying it was pulling out of Colombia because of mounting guerrilla unrest across the country.
"We're not planning to leave," Tom Melsen, head of all Amoco operations in Colombia, said in a telephone interview.
He added that "the guerrilla problem is certainly getting worse" but said the company had no plans to abandon the oil-rich Andean nation because of it.
An unsourced report in the latest edition of Colombia's monthly financial news magazine Dinero said Amoco and Total of France were both planning on pulling out the country.

Spokesmen for French oil company Total, a partner in the giant Cusiana oil development in Colombia's eastern plains, could not be reached for immediate comment. But Melsen said he had "no earthly idea at all" what the story was based on.
Amoco has been operating in Colombia for about three years now. It has discovered natural gas but no major crude oil reservoirs so far.
Separately, Dave Tayrien, manager for government and public affairs at Amoco's Houston operations, says reports of pulling out in Colombia are "categorically untrue."
In fact, he said Amoco recently announced they were stepping up investments there with a large natural gas project involving drilling and pipelines as well as a power project in central Colombia.
Tayrien added Amoco is committed to Colombia and the projects in spite of escalation in sabotage.
